title: Boss Level 4: The Tested Quiz App
concepts: splitting a program into a data module, a rules module and an app
pure rule functions with no input() or print()
a list of dictionaries as quiz data
writing pytest tests before the code
stub functions whose body is only a docstring (they return None)
strip() and lower() to compare answers
letting tests judge AI-written code, and re-running every test after a fix

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Given Asha's eight tests, the AI's module (examples/ai/flawed/quiz_logic.py) is judged by those tests: the AI wrote percentage() as points // total * 100 and said the module passes all eight tests. Floor division gives 0 for 3 out of 4, so three tests fail: both percentage tests and the result line, which printed 0% Practise again. Dividing with / and rounding at the end, round(points / total * 100), makes all eight pass.

changes: The curriculum asks for a multi-module quiz app with scoring and a passing test suite. The project uses three modules (data, rules, app) and one pytest file with eight tests, written before the rules.
The project introduces one pytest option, --tb=no, so the failure lists fit on screen (pytest lists each failed test in its short summary by default); the debug step uses --tb=short from Chapter 19.
Every app test is a copy of quiz_app.py with its own typed answers, in examples/apptest, next to copies of the two modules it imports.

The stub module, the first rule, the AI's flawed module, the debug test and the AI's improve suggestion each live in their own folder with a copy of the tests, so every report in the project is a verified run.
outstanding_issues: pytest's separator lines stretch to the width of the terminal; the outputs in this chapter use a fixed width of 56 columns, and the run time in the last line changes on every run.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
